title: Create a GitHub Issue as an agent task contract
steps: Open the repository Issues tab and create a new issue.
State the goal, context links, exact scope, and out-of-scope areas.
Add required evidence: tests, scans, screenshots, PR summary, and rollback note.
Name the human approval points before assignment.
verify: Issue has acceptance criteria, not just a request.
Sensitive areas are explicitly out of scope or approval-gated.
The agent can infer done criteria without guessing.
examTrap: A vague issue such as “fix login” is not a safe agent task contract.

title: Assign work to Copilot cloud agent safely
steps: Assign the issue only after the task contract is clear.
Confirm the repository has instructions and a working validation path.
Expect work on a scoped Copilot branch or PR branch, not direct main changes.
Review the session log and draft PR before any merge decision.
verify: Agent cannot approve or merge its own PR.
Required workflows and branch protections still apply.
A human reviewer owns the final decision.
examTrap: Do not treat assignment to Copilot as approval to bypass PR review.

title: Review an agent-created pull request as evidence
steps: Read the PR summary and compare it with the original issue.
Inspect changed files for scope creep.
Open checks, logs, scans, and artifacts rather than trusting the summary.
Request changes when evidence is missing or a sensitive area changed.
verify: Diff matches task scope.
Required checks are present and passing.
CODEOWNERS or specialist reviewers are included where needed.
examTrap: The agent saying “done” is not evidence; the PR evidence trail is.

title: Use GitHub Actions logs and artifacts for validation
steps: Open the workflow run linked from the PR.
Inspect failing and passing jobs for useful signal.
Download or inspect artifacts when the workflow produces reports.
Classify failures as environment, tool, context, permission, or reasoning problems.
verify: Logs support the claimed outcome.
Artifacts are relevant to acceptance criteria.
Failures are not hidden by removing checks.
examTrap: A green check is useful, but you still need to know what the check actually validates.

title: Configure branch protection for agent-created work
steps: Protect the default branch.
Require pull request review before merge.
Require status checks that prove build, test, security, or policy expectations.
Restrict direct pushes or force pushes where appropriate.
verify: Agent work cannot land on main without PR review.
Required checks match real validation needs.
Sensitive repositories do not rely on informal review.
examTrap: Disabling branch protection to “let the agent work faster” is usually the wrong answer.

title: Use repository rulesets for layered controls
steps: Create a named ruleset with a clear purpose.
Target the branch or tag patterns that need protection.
Add rules such as required checks, approving reviews, or deployment requirements.
Use ruleset visibility to help contributors understand blocked actions.
verify: Rulesets cover the branches agents might target.
Rules are discoverable and auditable.
Multiple controls can layer without hidden gaps.
examTrap: Rulesets and branch protection are control mechanisms, not documentation-only reminders.

title: Route agent changes with CODEOWNERS
steps: Identify sensitive paths such as auth, payment, deployment, or compliance files.
Add CODEOWNERS entries for those paths.
Combine code-owner review with branch protection or rulesets.
Keep ownership current when teams or components change.
verify: Sensitive file changes request the correct reviewers.
A reviewer with write access can approve when required.
Ownership files are themselves protected.
examTrap: A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review unless paired with the right protection rule.

title: Gate deployments with GitHub environments
steps: Create an environment for production or sensitive deployment targets.
Add required reviewers and prevent self-review where needed.
Restrict branches or tags that can deploy.
Store environment secrets so they unlock only after protection rules pass.
verify: Deployment jobs wait for approval before accessing protected secrets.
Only permitted branches/tags can deploy.
Bypass rules are intentionally configured.
examTrap: Production deployment should not be just another agent tool call.

title: Write repository custom instructions for agentic development
steps: Document project structure, build/test commands, coding conventions, and validation expectations.
Add stop conditions for sensitive files, secrets, production, and destructive commands.
Use path-specific instructions for special areas.
Avoid conflicting personal, repository, organization, and agent instructions.
verify: Instructions tell Copilot how to validate work, not just how to style code.
Instructions do not contain secrets or temporary assumptions.
Path-specific rules load for the files they govern.
examTrap: Instructions are governance support, not a substitute for branch protection or review.

title: Configure MCP access with least privilege
steps: Decide whether the task needs tools or only context.
Prefer the remote GitHub MCP server for typical setup unless local hosting is required.
Enable only the toolsets needed for the task.
Document which tools are read-only and which can write issues, branches, PRs, or comments.
verify: Tool access matches the task.
Write-capable tools have approval or branch boundaries.
MCP use is logged in the task or PR evidence.
examTrap: MCP is not harmless context; tools can change GitHub state.

title: Review agent session logs and audit evidence
steps: Open the agent session linked from commits or the PR.
Review the agent plan, tool use, changes, and failure handling.
Compare session claims with PR checks and artifacts.
Preserve links in the review notes for future audit.
verify: The session explains what the agent attempted and why.
Commits and PR discussion connect back to the human requester.
The evidence is enough for post-hoc analysis.
examTrap: If administrators cannot see what the agent did, the workflow is not accountable.

title: Track multi-agent handoffs in GitHub artifacts
steps: Give each agent a role and write scope.
Require a handoff comment or artifact after each stage.
Record decisions, changed files, evidence, risks, and next required action.
Pause or escalate when handoffs conflict.
verify: No two agents silently own the same file or decision.
Handoffs are visible in GitHub, not only chat.
Conflict resolution is recorded before merge.
examTrap: Parallel agents without handoff rules create speed-shaped confusion.
